metadata.title: Suno, Part Three.
metadata.audience: HAI Lyrical Literacy volunteers who have completed Parts 1 and 2. Internal training, not promotion.
metadata.narration_notes: SERIES FINALE — Part 1 says 'the first of three training videos', so this closes the set. BVDT recaps the SERIES, not this video; BHTF is a genuine close, not a Part-N tease. Host is Rohan V.; full name spoken EXACTLY ONCE, in BOUT. Phonetic spellings are deliberate for Kokoro G2P: 'Rohaan' = Row-Haan — do NOT 'correct' them. Register is internal volunteer training, never promotional; plan tiers are named as the UI shows them and never sold. Every SunoL3* scene must pass kicker='LYRICAL LITERACY · SUNO TUTORIAL PART 3' to SceneFrame; the kit default says PART 1. Built against SUNO-UI-SPEC.md §9-10. Heteronym pass done.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Rohaan from Humanitarians AI. This is Part 3, the last one. You can already make a song and drive the Advanced panel. This video is the ring around it — what you can bring into a track, and what you can do with one once you have it.

show.event: Composer fades up; serif greeting 'Hi, HAI' above it
The ask types itself into the composer
Send arms terracotta; running indicator appears
Three result lines reveal — bring in, work on, take out

props.command: I can make a song and drive the panel. What else is there?
output: Bring in: audio, a voice, or a playlist of your own songs.
Work on: Remix makes a new song, Edit changes this one.
Take out: MP3 — and more on Pro.

beats.act: Act 1 — executive summary (BLUF): in, and out
beats.narration_text: Here is the whole idea. Everything left sits on one of two sides of the panel you already know. On the way in, three buttons let you attach your own material. On the way out, a menu on every track decides what happens next. Both ends return to the same Advanced panel.

shot.new_visual_element: Two-sided map — attach row feeding IN, the track menu leading OUT, panel in the middle

show.event: The Advanced panel sits centre as a compact block, labelled from Part 2
On 'the way in', the attach row lights on the left with three feeds arrowing into the panel
On 'the way out', a finished track and its menu light on the right
A return arrow draws from the menu back into the panel — both ends are the same surface

props.sparkLine: In one side, out the other.

beats.narration_text: Above the Lyrics box sit three buttons. Add Audio takes a file — browse, upload, or record straight in. Add Voice picks a saved voice. Add Inspo points at one of your own playlists, and only your own music is used. Attach audio and the Inspo button steps aside, because the track is now the reference.

shot.new_visual_element: The attach row, each button opening its own surface in turn

show.event: Panel opens on Advanced; the attach row above Lyrics rules and highlights
+ Audio opens its dropdown — Browse, Upload, Record
+ Voice opens the voice picker: My Voices and Favorites, saved voices below
+ Inspo opens the playlist picker; the 'only your music' line highlights
Audio attaches — the row collapses to two buttons as Inspo steps aside

beats.narration_text: Inside the voice picker is Create a Voice, still marked Beta. Record a sample or upload one, and Suno uses it to shape how your songs sing. Four things matter: sing in the style you want, record at least ten seconds, find a quiet spot, and a decent microphone helps — though your laptop will do.

shot.new_visual_element: The Create a Voice modal with its Beta badge, three inputs and four tip cards

show.event: Voice picker open; the Create Voice row highlights and the modal opens over it
The Beta badge beside the title pulses once — this one will move
Record, Upload Audio and Select from library light in turn
The four tip cards resolve beneath
The ten-second rule rules terracotta — the only hard requirement

beats.narration_text: The third tab is Sounds, and it does not make songs. It makes short samples — effects, loops and one-shots. One field describes the sound you want. Its own Advanced Options hold three controls: Type, either a one-shot or a loop; then BPM and Key, both of which you can leave on automatic.

shot.new_visual_element: The Sounds tab — banner, Sound field, and its own Advanced Options

show.event: Active pill slides from Advanced to Sounds; the panel repopulates
The banner reads: short samples — effects, loops, one-shots
The Sound field takes focus: 'Describe the sound you want'
Advanced Options expands — note the label differs from the Advanced tab's More Options
Type toggles One-Shot to Loop; BPM and Key show their Auto and Any defaults

beats.narration_text: Now the other side. Every track carries a three-dot menu, and it is where everything after generation lives. Ten entries, split down the middle. Five open a submenu — Remix, Edit, Share, Download and Manage. The other five act at once: publish it, queue it, add it to a playlist, start a radio station, or send it to the trash.

shot.new_visual_element: The full ten-item track menu, submenu carets marked

show.event: A finished track row; the three-dot control highlights and the menu opens
All ten entries stand; ordinals count them out
The FIVE carrying a caret ring — Remix, Edit, Share, Download, Manage
The other five light as a group — they act on the spot

beats.narration_text: Remix and Edit look alike and are not. Remix makes a new song from this one — a cover in another genre, a mashup, a sample. Edit changes this song: extend it, crop it, remove a section, reverse it, slow it down. And picking either does the same thing — it reopens the Advanced panel with your track attached.

shot.new_visual_element: The two dropdown groups side by side, then both arrowing back into the Advanced panel

show.event: The mode dropdown opens showing both groups, REMIX above EDIT
REMIX group lights: Cover, Mashup, Sample, Inspo — each a NEW song
EDIT group lights: Extend, Crop, Remove Section, Reverse, Speed — the SAME song
Pro and Premier badges resolve on the entries that carry them
Both groups arrow down into the Advanced panel — the Part 2 callback

props.sparkLine: A new song, or this one.

beats.narration_text: Extend is the one you will reach for most, and it is worth seeing properly. Your track loads into the panel as attached audio, with the mode set to Extend. The waveform splits in two: the part you keep, and the part Suno recreates. Drag the boundary to say where the new material starts, then press Create.

shot.new_visual_element: The panel in Extend mode — KEEP and RECREATE regions, and the Extend-from point

show.event: Panel opens with the track attached; mode dropdown reads Extend
The waveform splits: magenta KEEP on the left, hatched RECREATE on the right
Both regions label themselves as the voice names them
The boundary drags; the Extend-from timestamp counts as it moves
Create arms into its warm gradient — the armed state

beats.narration_text: Last, getting it out. Download opens four choices. MP3 is the plain one and needs nothing extra — that is the file you hand in. WAV gives you a lossless master, Get Stems splits the track into its individual parts, and Video renders it for posting. Those three carry a Pro badge.

shot.new_visual_element: The Download submenu, four rows, badges as the UI shows them

show.event: Download highlights in the track menu and its submenu opens
MP3 Audio lights first, unbadged — the default path
WAV Audio, Get Stems and Video resolve with their Pro badges
MP3 rules terracotta as the one to use for handing work in

props.sparkLine: MP3 is the one you need.

beats.narration_text: The whole series, in one place. Sign in with Discord. Describe a song in Simple mode and let it run. Move to Advanced when the words matter. Attach audio, a voice or a playlist when you want your own material in it. Then use the track menu to extend, remix, or download what you made.

show.event: Artifact page resolves on the cream stage
Each line reveals as the voice reaches it — the series end to end

props.artifactHeading: The whole series, end to end
artifactLines: Sign in at suno.com with Discord.
Simple mode: one sentence — style + mood + topic. Two versions come back.
Advanced: Lyrics, Styles as comma-separated tags, then More Options.
Remix makes a NEW song from this one. Edit changes THIS one — Extend lives here.
Extend: drag the KEEP / RECREATE boundary, then Create.
Download → MP3 Audio. WAV, Stems and Video are Pro.

beats.narration_text: That is the whole tool. Across three videos you have gone from never having used Suno to signing in, writing a description on purpose, driving every control in the Advanced panel, and getting a finished file out. Everything after this is practice. Make something for your project this week, and keep the ones that surprise you.

show.event: Composer returns; greeting reads 'That is the whole tool.'
The closing question types into the composer
Three lines reveal — what the viewer can now do, end to end

props.command: What can I do now that I could not before?
output: Sign in, describe a song, and get two versions back.
Write lyrics and styles yourself, and set every control.
Extend, remix, and export a finished track.
